solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

blocks.note: post = after, the Latin prefix in 'postwar'
the numeral written as a word

annotation.surface: An instruction about something delayed until after the first page.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like a link word placing 'Put off' after page 1, but it is the first chunk of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: To postpone something is to put it off to a later time.

entries.clue: Advance showing of pupil’s first report (7)

blocks.note: a review is a critical report

annotation.surface: A school report handed over early, before the term ends.
annotation.walkthrough: The school setting makes 'report' look like a pupil's report card; here it is a review, as of a film or play.
annotation.definitionFit: A preview is a showing of a film or play before its general release.

entries.clue: Follow on to take legal action about case of embezzling (5)

indicatorNotes.about: SUE goes around the other letters
indicatorNotes.case of: a word's case is its outside: the first and last letters

blocks.note: to sue is to take legal action

annotation.surface: Following up an embezzlement case by going to court.
annotation.walkthrough: The legal surface makes 'case' a court case, but here a word's case is its outside, the letters that hold the rest in.
annotation.definitionFit: To segue is to follow on smoothly from one thing to the next.

entries.clue: Porters once worked somewhere in Westminster Abbey (5,6)

indicatorNotes.worked: the letters are worked into a new shape

annotation.surface: Hall porters who used to be employed at Westminster Abbey.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a job history; 'worked' is the anagram signal. Westminster Abbey is the London church where monarchs are crowned.
annotation.definitionFit: Poets' Corner is the part of Westminster Abbey where many writers are buried or commemorated.

annotation.surface: Cleaning up a canteen that isn't open yet, with shifts on the rota.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shifts' looks like work shifts in the canteen; it is a verb telling the letters to move.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean putting things in order, as in neatening a room or tidying a desk.

blocks.note: J = jack, as on playing cards
to ail is to feel unwell

annotation.surface: A worried question: might Jack be feeling ill?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Can' reads as the verb opening a question; it is a noun, American slang for prison.
annotation.definitionFit: Mainly American slang: someone locked up is 'in the can', just as they would be in prison.

indicatorNotes.converted: the letters are changed into another form

annotation.surface: A shop that has nearly finished being turned into a studio.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a property conversion, so 'converted' and 'almost' seem to describe the building work.
annotation.definitionFit: A French borrowing for a workshop, used in English for the workroom of a painter or couturier.

indicatorNotes.delivered: a speech is delivered, so the word is spoken

blocks.note: a list is a catalogue; said out, it matches the composer's name

annotation.surface: A composer's catalogue of works that has arrived in the post.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Delivered' suggests a parcel, but it means spoken, as a speech is delivered. The ’s stands for 'is': the composer is a catalogue, spoken.
annotation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian composer and pianist.

entries.clue: Bird, say, straddling a large egg to begin with (5)

indicatorNotes.straddling: EG sits astride A, one letter on each side

blocks.note: the word itself, straddled by EG
L = large, as on clothes labels

annotation.surface: A bird sitting astride a big egg to hatch it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for instance' introducing a bird, but it gives EG. E(A)G, then L and E, builds EAGLE.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the eagle is one particular species, a large hunting raptor.

indicatorNotes.heading off: the head, the first letter, comes off

annotation.surface: Athletes setting off to confront a crowd of protesters.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' reads as going to intercept the demonstrators; it means decapitating MARCHERS.
annotation.definitionFit: Archers compete in the sport of archery.

entries.clue: Church beginning to rely on old chart and timer (11)

annotation.surface: A church starting to depend on an antique chart and a clock.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a vicar's inventory; the answer is five small pieces strung together.
annotation.definitionFit: A chronograph is a watch or instrument for timing intervals, a stopwatch.

indicatorNotes.half-abandoned: half the word, its first three letters, is left out

annotation.surface: A general strike that has been partly called off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'General strike' is a stock phrase, so 'General' hides as an adjective; it is the soldier. Ike was the nickname of General Dwight D. Eisenhower.
annotation.definitionFit: Ike was General Eisenhower, Allied commander in the Second World War.

indicatorNotes.worried: the letters are worried, shaken into disorder
indicatorNotes.about: the jumbled letters go around the note

blocks.note: mi is a note of the sol-fa scale, set inside the jumbled letters after their fifth

annotation.surface: A boy called Herb whose parents are anxious about a letter from school.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Herb’s' looks like a man's name with a possessive; it is the definition, and ’s means 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: Spearmint is a common garden mint, a herb.

entries.clue: Move about with difficulty, with permit (6)

annotation.surface: Struggling to get around, even with a permit.
annotation.walkthrough: The second 'with' looks like a mere joining word; it supplies the W.
annotation.definitionFit: To wallow is to roll or flounder about clumsily, as in mud or heavy seas.

entries.clue: Song title changed by Elvis originally (3,2,2)

blocks.note: first letters of by and Elvis

annotation.surface: A song whose name Elvis Presley altered.
annotation.walkthrough: 'By' looks like it names who made the change, but it is fodder: 'originally' takes the first letter of both 'by' and 'Elvis'. The song is by the Beatles.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Beatles released it in 1970 as one of their last singles.

entries.clue: Dish made of hollowed-out European elm? (6)

indicatorNotes.hollowed-out: the inside is removed, leaving the first and last letters

blocks.note: an elm is an example of a tree; the question mark flags it

annotation.surface: A bowl carved from a hollowed trunk of a European elm.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is woodwork; 'hollowed-out' applies to the word 'European', not the elm.
annotation.definitionFit: An entrée is a dish, a course served at a meal.

entries.clue: Rubbish on site initially affecting country (7)

indicatorNotes.Rubbish: as a verb or adjective, the letters are trashed into disorder

blocks.note: first letter of affecting, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: Waste dumped at a site is harming a whole nation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' looks like the subject of the sentence, a pile of waste; it signals the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the northernmost of the three Baltic states, with Tallinn as its capital.

indicatorNotes.lodging in: the answer lodges inside the following words

annotation.surface: An Irishman staying in a town in Ireland finds it funny.
annotation.walkthrough: Portlaoise is a real Irish town, which keeps the surface honest while the answer spans its end and the next word.
annotation.definitionFit: Seamus is an Irish man's name.

entries.clue: Pioneer of press corporation introduces book in new genre (9)

indicatorNotes.introduces: the rearranged letters take B inside them
indicatorNotes.new: the letters of 'genre' are made new

blocks.note: a corporation is jokey old slang for a pot belly, a gut

annotation.surface: A media corporation launching a book in a new literary genre.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Press corporation' reads as a newspaper company; 'corporation' is also old slang for a paunch. Gutenberg invented printing with movable type.
annotation.definitionFit: Johannes Gutenberg pioneered the printing press in 15th-century Germany.

annotation.surface: A verdict that a kind of English music is awful.
annotation.walkthrough: Grime is a genre of electronic music that emerged in London in the early 2000s.
annotation.definitionFit: Grime is a style of British dance and rap music.

indicatorNotes.from behind: read the word starting from its back end

blocks.note: a tab is a bill, as in a bar tab

annotation.surface: Someone called Bill struck from behind in an attack.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bill' is capitalised to look like a man's name; it is an invoice.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: batting a ball away or batting at a fly both mean striking it.

entries.clue: Reportedly what Cupid uses to shoot sweethearts (5)

indicatorNotes.Reportedly: as it is said, not written

blocks.note: Cupid shoots arrows from a bow

annotation.surface: Word has it Cupid uses something to shoot lovers with his arrows.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sweethearts' seems to be Cupid's target; it is the definition, and the French plural beaux matches the sound of 'bows'.
annotation.definitionFit: The French plural of beau, used in English for male admirers or suitors, a lady's gentlemen callers.

indicatorNotes.undergoing refurbishment: the letters are being refitted into a new order

annotation.surface: Stations closed for renovation, with makeshift arrangements in place.
annotation.walkthrough: The railway surface makes 'Temporary' sound like a stopgap timetable; it is the definition alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as adjectives: an interim manager or report holds the fort until a permanent one arrives.

blocks.note: an aga was an Ottoman commander or official

annotation.surface: An Ottoman leader who has regained public favour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Once more' seems to tie to 'popular' as a comeback; it is the definition by itself.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'try again' and 'try once more' say the same, both marking a repeat.

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word, all but the last letter

blocks.note: the 100m sprint is an example of an athletics event

annotation.surface: A 100-metre sprint run on a track that is nearly level.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flat' fits the running track, where flat races are a category; here it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Even and flat both describe a level surface.

entries.clue: Has pyxie briefly withered with a lack of oxygen (8)

indicatorNotes.briefly: the word is cut short, losing its last letter
indicatorNotes.withered: the letters are shrivelled out of shape

annotation.surface: A pyxie plant that has shrivelled for want of air.
annotation.walkthrough: Pyxie is a low evergreen shrub of the American pine barrens, so a withered one fits the surface; the E comes off before the mix.
annotation.definitionFit: Asphyxia is suffocation, the body being starved of oxygen.
